$comment: Level 12 (pacing pass 2): Forge mode on a 160 map. After the Forge the turtle rival (hard, 18 troops, towers, posted guards, no worshippers for 15 minutes so it keeps its people) sits behind its moat and sends a war band every four minutes from minute 8. Wolf dens haunt the central plain; clearing them raises the middle ward (prayer chain), holding all three stones raises a seer stone on the north hill that the digger can reach as easily, and winning it draws a war band onto your home ward. Staged: clear two dens, hold three stones 60 s, win the hill seer stone, gain 30 followers over the count you had when the seer fell (fromStage, so a big early tribe still has to grow) under the raids, then raze the Hearth once twelve posted guards dig in around it. Bot wins about 19000 (followers stage 8500 to 14500).
name: The Forge
description: Before the battle, both tribes reshape the land around their Hearths. Raise walls or dig a moat, then press Ready. Clear two wolf dens, hold three stones, win the hill seer stone, gain 30 more followers under the digger's raids, then cross its moat and raze its Hearth.

rewards.text: The home ley pays mana while you hold it.
The home ward guards your southern flank.
The middle ward commands the road to the moat.
The hill seer stone looks over the digger's moat.

objectives.text: Clear both wolf dens on the plain
Pray at the risen middle ward and hold all three stones at once for a minute
Win the seer stone risen on the north hill before the digger does
Gain 30 more followers while the digger's war bands cross the plain
Cross the moat, break the posted guards and raze the digger's Hearth

do.text: The Forge is over. Flatten or Raise Land can bridge a moat. Wolves hold the central plain.
The digger sends a war band across the plain.
With the wolves gone, the middle ward rises on the plain. The digger wants it too.
A seer stone rises on the north hill, as near the digger as it is to you.
The digger answers the seer stone: a war band marches on your home ward.
The digger digs in: posted guards now ring its Hearth behind the moat.
